target_problem: instantiate a published algorithm-to-circuit-lower-bound transfer using the inherited Range-Avoidance engine after the CHR/Li advances
conditional_implication: If the inherited engine were extended from low-support-branchwidth promises to a total, all-instance, single-valued Range-Avoidance algorithm in the exact circuit representation required by a checked transfer theorem, with the theorem-required size and running-time parameters, then the cited transfer could yield its stated circuit lower bound.
frontier_reason: Li already closes the natural depth-3 Missing-String target, while the inherited engine is polynomial only under a severe width promise and supplies no total high-width branch.

current_gap: The first missing bridge is all-instance coverage: the current algorithm is polynomial only for support branchwidth O(sqrt(log m)), and its high-width branch has no canonical avoided-string output.
result_obtained: A theorem-by-theorem post-Li calibration, executable finite reproduction of the Korten/GGM decoding kernel, erratum enforcement, barrier audit, and a parameter-level no-go for the inherited width engine.
stop_rule: Close the Williams/Missing-String transfer branch for the inherited width-promised engine unless an all-instance completion, a checked still-open transfer target, or an explicit nonalgebrizing ingredient is supplied.
